findings.text: - the plan records a search only for the scheduler verbs and never opens the admission path in reckon/crew/dispatch.py, so it proposes a new binding bound without naming the mechanism that already decides what may be dispatched. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes. REASON: the plan's claim that the roster is the only concurrency authority is a prior-art statement the code refutes, so running the search changes how sections 3 and 5 are written.

- sections 3 and 5 add a reservation roster cap as a concurrency ceiling, but a concurrency ceiling already owns this decision in _refuse_over_concurrency_ceiling, whose own docstring says the retired roster key never binds. The plan asserts the opposite of the owner beside it. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes. REASON: two concurrency ceilings with no text reconciling them leave a reader unable to tell which is authoritative; the plan should extend the bound model in dispatch.py or say why the roster is a distinct third axis.

- the placement's roster population is derived by roster_occupants over the live-pointer list, duplicating the live-run population the admission path already builds in _live_runs_across_backends at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:600. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes. REASON: a second reader of the live-placed population can drift from the first on which projects and which liveness reading count.

- section 1 introduces a PlacementConfig definition and the requirements, state_query and reason_query field family plus a job-id field on the run record, and says only that this is an addition rather than a difference in shape. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes. REASON: the section grows a public interface family without naming a definition it retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be.

- section 3 adds a reckon crew placement CLI option and states only that it mirrors reckon crew watch --ensure, which is reuse of a pattern, not a retirement or merge of the option it adds. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes. REASON: the section adds to cli_options, 317 this week, without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass. The placement machinery hides the reservation lifecycle, its publication path, the roster count and the refusal text behind ensure_reservation, read_reservation, reservation_step_* and roster_occupants. Consumers call those rather than re-deriving any of it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding. The plan mints a second concurrency ceiling, the reservation roster, in reckon/crew/placement.py beside the existing one in reckon/crew/dispatch.py, and never names the existing owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding. Counts: public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23. Section 1 adds a PlacementConfig definition and a new job-id field on the run record without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be. Section 3 adds a reckon crew placement CLI option the same way.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding. The plan searched only for srun, sbatch and SLURM, and for the launch path. It never opens the existing admission path in reckon/crew/dispatch.py that already bounds worker population, so it asserts prior art the code refutes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass. The wrap prefixes the already-resolved argv, and the plan states the interface is carried through unchanged with absence meaning today's login-node launch. That is the justification the item asks for.
